Approach step 3 and the rollback plan have the deploy job run the migrate CLI's down step against the production database when the post-deploy health check fails. The up migration only adds a nullable column, so the previous image already runs against the extra column. Dropping it is unnecessary and destructive. Labels written by the new release during the health-check window are lost, and ac-labels-returned would silently stop holding for those runs. The down step also races with live traffic from the new image, which still writes and reads labels while the column is being dropped. Redeploying the previous image alone, leaving the additive column in place, would back the release out safely. If the plan keeps schema rollback, it must justify it and handle data loss and ordering.

Step 3 of the approach and the rollback plan, in deploy/scripts/release-deploy.sh. On a failed health check the job runs the migrate CLI's down step against production first, and only then redeploys the previous image. For that window the new image is still serving and its queries select or insert the labels column, so dropping the column breaks it, and the plan does not address this. The down step also permanently destroys every label written between deploy and failure, which is the data the feature exists to capture. An unattended destructive production migration is not a realistic rollback for an additive nullable column. The old image does not need the column dropped, so the rollback can simply redeploy the previous image and leave the column in place. At minimum the plan must reorder the steps (redeploy first, then migrate down only if truly needed) and state the data-loss tradeoff.
